correctness.rationale: The Zak transform diagonalizes the critical Bessel-system operator; there is no positive lower frame bound and no ordinary trace assertion. Splitting the exponential Zak series at k=0 and summing both geometric parts gives the displayed transform. The multiplier simplifies with b=sin²(θ/2) and D=4q(h²+b): L=a h²(1−b)/(h²+b)², E=a/(h²+b)>0 and U=a h²(1+h²)/(h²+b)². Both L and U decrease strictly on [0,π], and s grows strictly in y=|x−1/2|>0. Pushing the y-density 2 through L+E sinh²(ay) gives the stated conditional factor 1/[a√((s−L)(s−L+E))], then averaging θ gives the law; unitarity gives mean one. Continuity on the torus and positive local area in every interior band give full support. The four levels are the endpoints and the stated interior saddle and seam levels; h⁴=1+h² has the unique positive h²=φ. At the minimum the quadratic coefficients in x and θ are a³/c² and a h²/(4c⁴); area normalization gives 1/(2√(αβ)) as stated. At the saddle they are a²s_a and −s_a(1/4+2q/(1−q)²); changing the rescaled Morse coordinates X,Y to X±Y gives coefficient 1/(2π√(a²s_a γ)) for log(1/|s−s_a|) on either side. At the seam the inward normal slope magnitude is E·a sinh a and the angular curvature magnitude in the expansion is 2Uq/(1∓q)² at θ=0 or π respectively. The two normal sides give local conditional density 2/A, measured against dθ/(2π). Thus the allowed interval near the maximum, or the deleted interval above the seam minimum, of length 2√(ε/B)+O(ε^(3/2)), gives respectively the stated upper-edge constant and the negative cusp. Away from the saddle a local extension across the seam gives a regular background via the nonzero normal derivative. Smooth-cell regular-value contributions are smooth, and the bounded seam term cannot change the saddle logarithm at coincidence. This establishes the statements for the canonical density representative; the exact integral is an a.e. density.
residual_risks: Frozen replays are python checker.py (NumPy) and python density_validation.py (NumPy and SciPy), not executed here. Recorded checks compare finite series and constants, and sample the seam law at a=1 and 3. They do not certify all parameters. The analytic check covers the continuum and the coincidence case.

Frame operator is understood in the Bessel-system sense S=TT*, not as a claim that the critical system is a frame. At the crossover only the logarithmic leading law with bounded remainder is asserted. No pointwise uniqueness of an a.e. density is intended.

value.rationale: For a canonical exponentially localized window, the normalized law gives distributional conditioning information beyond the operator’s essential range, and provides exact coefficients for qualitatively different singularities. In particular it distinguishes a smooth saddle from a seam-induced cusp, shows exactly when their order reverses, and fixes which leading singularity survives at the coincident level. These are useful precise invariants of the natural Zak normalization rather than an arbitrary parameter sample.
residual_risks: Applies only to the specified unit-square critical lattice and normalized area law. No noncritical-lattice stability, trace formula, or sharper uniform two-parameter crossover asymptotic is established.
